# `x4compat`

```text
usage: x4compat [-h] [--version] {check} ...

Detect how the ENABLED (active) X4 mods collide over the effective XML tree -- the set the engine
loads: on disk in any configured extensions root and enabled (the profile entry decides; the
manifest's enabled= is only the default when the profile has none), with every required dependency
loading.

positional arguments:
  {check}
    check     analyze collisions across the enabled (active) modlist

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --version   show program's version number and exit
```

## `x4compat check`

```text
usage: x4compat check [-h] [--ext-dir EXT_DIR] [--reference REFERENCE] [--soft] [--json]
                      [candidate]

A replace/remove landing on content ANOTHER mod added fails (HARD) unless the overwriting mod
declares a DIRECT dependency (required or optional, matched by the adder's manifest id, not its
folder name) on that mod: then it is an intended patch, reported as an advisory grouped per mod
pair (every row in --json dependent_overwrites). A dependency of a dependency does not count, and
two mods overwriting the same added node still fail.

positional arguments:
  candidate             the mod to focus on ('before I add this'): an existing folder PATH is the
                        copy analysed (a same-named copy in the extensions dir is then left out);
                        a bare NAME means the copy in the extensions dir. Omit it to analyse every
                        enabled mod

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --ext-dir EXT_DIR     scan ONLY this extensions dir (default: every configured root -- game-root
                        extensions\, the profile's extensions\ and the Steam Workshop folder, from
                        _registry)
  --reference REFERENCE
                        unpacked base+DLC reference tree ($X4_REFERENCE)
  --soft                also list benign SOFT overlaps
  --json                machine-readable output
```
